create.name: Sakya Tsechen Ling
create.bio:
Sakya Tsechen Ling, also known as the European Institute of Tibetan Buddhism, is a Sakya temple in the Alsatian village of Kuttolsheim, west of Strasbourg. It grew from a group started in Strasbourg in 1977 by the Tibetan master Khenchen Sherab Gyaltsen Amipa Rinpoche, who had been sent to Switzerland in the 1960s to serve Tibetan refugees; the centre moved to Kuttolsheim the following year and was inaugurated by His Holiness the Sakya Trizin. The Dalai Lama visited in 1982. For more than twenty-five years Khenpo Dakpa Woeser lived here as resident lama, and since Khenchen Sherab's death in 2014 his chosen successor, Khenpo Tashi Sangpo, has guided the European centres he founded.

The core of the programme is a monthly weekend of teachings, running from Friday evening to Sunday afternoon and often including an initiation. Between those weekends there are Saturday afternoon gatherings for listening, reflection and meditation, and themed study series. The temple also marks the great Buddhist festivals and holds summer and winter retreats. Several sessions can be followed on Zoom, including the Dharma Chakra Program, a multi-year study of classical Buddhist philosophy given in English by the 42nd Sakya Trizin, with interpretation into other European languages.

courses.title: Buddha Manjushri: teachings and initiation with Khenpo Tashi Sangpo
courses.description: A monthly weekend session at the Kuttolsheim temple on Manjushri, the Buddha of wisdom, with teachings and an initiation: Friday evening, then Saturday and Sunday mornings and afternoons. On site only, with no video broadcast.

courses.title: Dharma Chakra Program: classical Buddhist philosophy
courses.description: A five-year study programme in which Ratna Vajra Rinpoche, the 42nd Sakya Trizin, teaches in English, moving from Abhidharma through the Way of the Bodhisattva to Madhyamaka and the Uttaratantra. Two Tuesday evenings a month on Zoom or in person at the sister centre in Arosio, Switzerland; open to all, with interpretation available.

free_resources.title: Monthly teaching weekends
free_resources.description: How the temple's monthly teaching weekends run: Friday evening, then Saturday and Sunday mornings and afternoons, with registration through the secretariat about two weeks ahead.
